tagline: First Mercury orbiter — 6 planetary gravity assists over 6.6 years to bleed energy before insertion in 2011
description: NASA Discovery-class MErcury Surface, Space ENvironment, GEochemistry, and Ranging mission. Launched 2004-08-03 on a Delta II 7925H-9.5. The 6.6-year cruise used 6 gravity assists (1 Earth, 2 Venus, 3 Mercury) to lose ~5 km/s of heliocentric energy — direct orbit insertion would have needed impossible delta-v. Mercury orbit insertion 2011-03-18; mapped the planet for 4 years. Discoveries: water ice in permanently shadowed polar craters, organic-rich dark material at the poles, exosphere composition, a magnetic field offset from the planet centre, abundant hollow-bottomed pits. Impacted Mercury 2015-04-30 after exhausting propellant — left a 16 m artificial crater near the north pole.
best_known_for: First Mercury orbiter — 4 years mapping the planet, ended in controlled impact 2015-04-30
